# Job Offer Process Map
::: {.cs-hook}
Two phases, five lanes. Application runs every day and has one gate, owned by
the candidate. Interview is triggered by an invite and repeats once per round,
and every gate has two keys: the hiring side's and the candidate's.
:::
:::

::: {.process-map}

## Frame

```{=html}
<div class="frames">
  <div class="frame"><b>Stage-Gate</b><span>Structure. Stages hold the work, gates hold the decisions. Outcomes: go, hold, kill, recycle.</span></div>
  <div class="frame"><b>BPMN swimlanes</b><span>Notation. Lanes show who does each step; crossing a lane is a handoff.</span></div>
  <div class="frame"><b>PDCA</b><span>The round loop. Prep is Plan, interview is Do, retrospective is Check, next prep is Act.</span></div>
</div>
<div class="legend">
  <span><i class="lg-evt"></i>event</span>
  <span><i class="lg-gate"></i>gate</span>
  <span><i></i>activity</span>
  <span><i class="lg-dash"></i>conditional or loop</span>
</div>
```

```{=html}
  <li><b>Submit</b> (Candidate). On the employer's own board, never an aggregator.</li>
  <li><span class="tag evt-t">Event</span><b>Application submitted.</b> Handoff to Interview.</li>
```

```{=html}
<ol class="steps">
  <li><span class="tag evt-t">Event</span><b>Invite</b> (recruiter). Message event, picked up by the email monitor.</li>
  <li><b>Schedule</b> (Candidate). Accept, share availability.</li>
  <li><b>Prep docs</b> (Claude). Plan: prep doc to read before, call doc open during.</li>
  <li><b>Interview</b> (Candidate with the recruiter on the screener, the hiring side after that). Do: recorded with consent, transcribed. Portfolio walk in hiring manager and panel rounds, never the screener. Confirm the timeline before hanging up.</li>
  <li><b>Retrospective</b> (Claude). Check: what landed, what to cut, what they were hanging on.</li>
  <li><span class="tag gate-t">Gate</span><b>Build check</b> (Candidate). Asked every round. On a yes, Claude builds it and it ships to the hiring side, where it can inform their decision. On a no, the round goes straight to the gate.</li>
  <li><span class="tag gate-t">Gate</span><b>Dual-key gate.</b> Hiring side: advance or reject, after a wait. Candidate: continue or withdraw, based on their burning questions.</li>
  <li><span class="tag evt-t">Event</span><b>Withdraw</b>. The candidate turns the key: the process ends on the candidate's side.</li>
  <li><b>Next round</b>. Act: back to prep with what the retrospective found.</li>
  <li><span class="tag evt-t">Event</span><b>Offer</b>. Exits to negotiation and the accept/decline decision, both out of scope.</li>
  <li><span class="tag evt-t">Event</span><b>Reject</b>, then <b>Follow-up</b>: warm email, ship any build in progress.</li>
  <li><span class="tag evt-t">Event</span><b>Recycle</b>. A new invite re-enters Phase 2 directly and skips Application.</li>
</ol>
<p class="hint">Not drawn: the timer event when a promised timeline passes, which gives a legitimate reason to make contact again.</p>
```

## Build decision rule {#build-rule}

```{=html}
<div class="rule">
<dl>
  <dt>Must-meet</dt><dd>An application exists. Someone on their side has named a problem in their own words. A plan-shaped answer can ship before the next gate.</dd>
  <dt>Should-meet</dt><dd>The problem was confirmed when the candidate asked about it. It touches something on the resume, such as governance. It's a later round.</dd>
  <dt>Backstop</dt><dd>At least one build per process. If none has fired by the last known round, force one.</dd>
  <dt>Ship rule</dt><dd>Confirmed: ship later, in their language. Not confirmed: ship it anyway, framed as "this might not be it."</dd>
</dl>
</div>
```

## Terms

```{=html}
<div class="rule">
<dl>
  <dt>JD</dt><dd>Job description: the employer's posting for the role.</dd>
  <dt>ATS</dt><dd>Applicant tracking system: the employer's hiring software, which parses submitted resumes. Different systems parse the same resume differently.</dd>
  <dt>Master resume</dt><dd>A long superset of every past role and result. Each tailored resume is cut down from it; nothing is written fresh.</dd>
  <dt>STAR library</dt><dd>A collection of past-work stories in Situation, Task, Action, Result form, reused across resumes, cover letters, application answers and interviews.</dd>
  <dt>Rule layer</dt><dd>The written rules for tailoring: what to claim, what not to claim, what never to do. Gaps are stated, never glossed.</dd>
  <dt>Resurfacing board</dt><dd>Where held postings wait to be reconsidered on a later day.</dd>
  <dt>Build</dt><dd>A piece of work made for one employer's named problem, usually a plan for how to solve it rather than a chart.</dd>
  <dt>Portfolio walk</dt><dd>A short live screen-share of past builds during a hiring manager or panel interview. Never on the screener.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
```
